description:
Lubliniec Castle, in the Silesian town of the same name, is first recorded in 1397, when it belonged to Władysław Opolczyk, Duke of Opole. Some sources trace the castle's origins back further, to the end of the 13th century, but the exact founding date remains uncertain, so the 1397 record is the firmest reference point available.

The castle remained associated with the Dukes of Opole, and its most notable recorded royal visit came in 1638, when King Władysław IV Vasa was received here. Over the centuries that followed, repeated renovations gave the castle its present Baroque appearance, replacing whatever earlier medieval character the building may have had.

Today Lubliniec Castle is privately owned and operates as a hotel, with a spa and a sauna area among its amenities.
